We have many templates. The first entry (reaction_id 1914385) seems to be a Diels-Alder type: It shows product is the bicyclic lactone, reactants are a diene and a carbonyl? Let's examine: mapped_rxn: '[CH2:6]=[CH:7][CH:8]=[CH2:9].[CH3:1][O:2][C:3](=[O:4])[C:5]1=[CH:10][C:11](=[O:12])[CH2:13]1>>[CH3:1][O:2][C:3](=[O:4])[C@:5]12[CH2:6][CH:7]=[CH:8][CH2:9][C@H:10]1[C:11](=[O:12])[CH2:13]2'

That looks like a Diels-Alder between a diene (CH2=CH-CH=CH2) and a dienophile (a carbonyl-containing alkene). The product matches our target? Our target SMILES: COC([C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O)=O. That is a methyl ester of a bicyclic lactone? The product in template: [CH3][O][C](=O)[C@]12[CH2][CH]=[CH][CH2][C@H]1[C](=O)[CH2]2. That seems similar but our target has a methyl ester attached to carbonyl? Actually product has methyl ester attached to carbonyl (COC(=O) ...). The template product has [CH3][O][C](=O) attached to the bicyclic core, same as ours. So this template likely matches.

We need to verify matching with our target SMILES. Use check_smiles_reaction_template_matching with template_id = 1914385 (but tool expects template_id as string). Let's do that.
